title: Checkout 500 spike: rollback approved by admin, verified, incident resolved
scenario: Simulator world 'checkout_bad_deploy' (OpsBench v2; same world and request as backend/app/demo/flagship.py). Operator request through POST /agent/investigate; admin approval through POST /approvals/{id}/approve.
providerNote: LLM_PROVIDER=groq, model openai/gpt-oss-120b (the provider/model OpsBench measured), running in the OpsPilot backend container; decisions are live model output.

run.user_request: Checkout failures increased after the latest deployment of checkout-api. Investigate and remediate if the evidence supports it.

knowledge.content: # Checkout Configuration Mismatch Postmortem The checkout-api 500 spike for incident PAY-451 followed deployment v3.8.2, which carried a different PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL from the production baseline. The strongest evidence was the CONFIG_MISMATCH log aligned with the deployment timestamp and increased 5xx rate. The corrective procedure is to compare rendered configuration with the approved baseline, identify the configuration owner, and verify the next deployment in the simulator. Do not infer a code regression from a 500 spike until configuration and dependency evidence have been checked.

# Payment Latency Runbook Use this runbook when payments-api latency rises above the simulator baseline. For incident PAY-442 on payments-api after version v3.8.2, confirm service health and request latency first. Compare the timestamp with the latest deployment and inspect database timeout logs. A database timeout is evidence of a dependency problem, not proof that the application code is defective. For a controlled response, preserve evidence, compare the deployment version with the previous known-good version, and check database pool saturation. Recommend rollback only when deployment timing and application evidence agree. Rollback is an approved action, never an automatic command.

# Deployment Rollback Runbook A rollback is considered only after a deployment is correlated with a new error or latency signal and the prior version is known. Confirm health, metrics, logs, and deployment history before proposing it. This document describes a recommendation procedure, not an execution authority. A human approval is required before any rollback. Capture the current version, target version, evidence timestamps, expected verification signal, and a safe stop condition.
